# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

# [tinydb] recent context, ⟦CMEM_NOW_HEADER:cefcb4b9df0d⟧
Mode: Code Development (code)

Legend: 🎯session ●bugfix ◆feature ↻refactor ✓change ○discovery ⚖decision ⚠security_alert ⚷security_note ⊘sensitive
Format: ID TIME TYPE TITLE
Fetch details: get_observations([IDs]) | Search: mem-search skill

Stats: 12 obs (4,991t read) | 82,468t work | 94% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
1 8:35p ○ Table read path re-reads storage on uncached searches; query cache is the only reuse
2 " ○ JSONStorage.read() parses the entire file on every call, and every write also starts with a full read
3 " ◆ Added scripts/bench_read.py benchmark for TinyDB read timing on a generated ~40MB database
4 " ○ json.load of the full file accounts for nearly all uncached search time on a 40.9MB database
S2 Benchmark TinyDB read performance on a ~40MB JSON database, confirm whether JSONStorage re-parses the whole file per query, attribute the time, and advise on caching options given the database lives on NFS. (Nov 3, 8:36 PM)
S1 Benchmark TinyDB read performance on a ~40MB JSON database, confirm whether JSONStorage re-parses the whole file per query, and attribute the time. (Nov 3, 8:36 PM)
5 8:36p ✓ Committed scripts/bench_read.py as 5ff1fbb "chore: add read benchmark script"
6 8:39p ○ All TinyDB table reads funnel through Table._read_table, so a cache there covers every read path
7 " ○ JSONStorage holds one open file handle and reads/writes through it, returning None for empty files
8 " ○ Table._update_table clears the query cache only after its own write, leaving external writes uncovered
9 8:40p ◆ JSONStorage now caches parsed data keyed by a content digest of the file
10 " ⚷ Cached parse results are shared objects that callers can mutate in place
11 " ○ Test suite passes with pytest-cov addopts disabled, and blake2b digesting dominates per-read cost
12 " ⚖ Freshness check switched from blake2b to length plus in-process string hash
S3 Cache JSON parses in TinyDB reads so repeated reads skip parsing when the file is unchanged, while keeping changes from the importer process visible. Benchmark and verify on a ~40 MB database. (Nov 3, 8:40 PM)
**Investigated**: Code paths in tinydb/storages.py (JSONStorage read/write and handle lifecycle) and tinydb/table.py (_read_table, _update_table, and every read and write call site). Ran scripts/bench_read.py on a generated 161,320-document, 40.9 MB database. Ran the test suite, which failed at first on pytest-cov addopts in pytest.ini and passed once addopts was cleared. Timed the cost of file read, encoding, and blake2b hashing on a 40 MB file.

**Learned**: Every Table read funnels through _read_table, and every write goes through _update_table, which does a full read before its write and clears the query cache afterward. Before the change, json.load took about 365 ms on the benchmark file, and blake2b hashing of 40 MB cost about 60 ms, which made it too expensive for a per-read check. Mtime and size are unreliable for freshness on NFS, so the check has to look at the file contents. Python's str hash is randomized per process, which is acceptable because the cache lives in one process.

**Completed**: JSONStorage now keeps a parse cache keyed by (length, hash of text). read() still reads the file each call but skips json.loads when the text is unchanged. write() stores the data it just wrote as the cache. Table._update_table invalidates the cache when an updater raises, and JSONStorage gained invalidate_cache(). Added tests/test_storages.py with two tests covering external same-length rewrites and failed updates. The full suite passes with 230 tests. Benchmark: storage.read() dropped from about 365 ms to 44 ms, and uncached search from about 340 ms to 72 ms. Changes are uncommitted in tinydb/storages.py, tinydb/table.py, and tests/test_storages.py.

**Next Steps**: Waiting for the user to decide whether to commit the current changes or to take on the cost of wrapping every dict in a Document, which dominates db.all() at about 326 ms and is not affected by this change.

**Notes**: The cache returns shared nested objects, so callers that mutate returned data will affect later reads. The (length, hash) check is non-cryptographic and could in principle miss a same-length edit that collides, which is negligible for a trusted importer. Benchmark numbers come from one local run and have not been measured on the NFS share. The remaining ~44 ms per read is the cost of reading and hashing the file, and a generation token written by the importer would be needed to remove it.


Access 82k tokens of past work via get_observations([IDs]) or mem-search skill.
